$comment: Findings from the estate-wide run of tools/estate-topics.mjs, each with the evidence, the
repository that can repair it, and WHY IT IS STILL HERE. None is fixable in micro-org, and every
one was invisible to the CI of the repository that holds it, because it is a disagreement between
two.
THIS IS NOT AN EXEMPTION LIST, and the difference is mechanical rather than a promise:
* an entry whose finding has been repaired FAILS the step — 'the record no longer describes
the estate, delete it' — so the file empties itself instead of rotting;
* a finding with no entry FAILS the step. Every instance that lands from today is red on the
day it lands. The ratchet is the point.
It is the UNPRODUCED_NOTIFICATIONS pattern (notify/src/topics.ts) applied where it has to live:
the only checkout that can see both halves. The alternative was a job that is red from its first
run for defects micro-org cannot fix, and beacon/src/estate.ts:15 records what happens to a gate
like that — 'a declared-but-skipping critical journey would refuse every release for ever', and
then somebody switches it off.
WHAT THE FIRST NINE TAUGHT THIS FILE, ALL OF IT WITHIN A DAY OF WRITING THEM:
1. `status` IS NEW, AND IT IS THE FIELD THAT WAS MISSING. All nine were written as 'found, and
somebody else must fix it'. Two were not that at all — settlement.outbound.failed and
market.offer.made are DECISIONS taken in micro-notify, which refuses to key a rule to an
envelope naming nobody it could address (`blockedBy: 'no-subject'`), and each needs one
field from the producer first. Recorded as omissions they read as neglect; recorded as
deferrals with an `until`, they read as what they are and they end when the condition does.
notify learned exactly this about its own records one file earlier. `deferred` requires
`until`, because a deferral with no end condition is an exemption with better manners.
2. EVIDENCE CAN BE WRONG, AND WAS. The record for custody.key.exported said custody's export
path 'completes in silence'. It did not: custody/src/exports.ts:422 was emitting
`custody.export.completed` — a name in no registry with no subscriber anywhere — while
`custody.key.exported` was named in seven places across five repositories including a
CRITICAL notify rule. Read as written the record pointed at 'add an emit'; the repair was a
rename in ONE repository. 'Nobody emits this' and 'somebody emits it under a name nobody
knows' are two findings with two repairs, and the checker now says which — it derives the
producer's unregistered emits and names them in the verdict, so nobody writes that evidence
wrongly again. Prose is not checkable; that is why as much of it as possible was moved into
something the checker derives.
3. RECORDS GO STALE IN HOURS, NOT MONTHS. Five of the nine were repaired the same night they
were written. The self-emptying property is not a nicety here, it is the normal case.
4. ONE RECORD CAN ABSORB MORE THAN ONE FINDING — suppression is by `<kind>:<topic>` alone, so
two repositories holding a rule for one unregistered topic are silenced by one entry whose
evidence describes one of them. Not narrowed (the second occurrence is the same defect, and
a red micro-org cannot fix is a red somebody switches off), but the run PRINTS every
absorbed finding, so the report is complete even where this file is not.
5. A DIRECTION THAT CANNOT BE RECORDED HAS EXACTLY ONE ESCAPE, AND IT IS THE BAD ONE.
Directions 1-4 went through `record()`; direction 5 — an emitter nothing calls — pushed
straight onto `errors`, so it was the one finding in this file that could carry no
evidence, no owner, no date and no `until`. Not a stricter check: a check whose only
answers were 'fix it' and 'switch the step off', which is the thing the paragraph above
about beacon/src/estate.ts:15 exists to warn about. It bit on tessera.object.anchored,
where the honest answer is neither — the producer cannot be called because a Solidity
contract has never been written four repositories away, while its consumer sits complete
and tested. The kind `unreachable` was added and direction 5 keyed BY TOPIC like every
other, which it could always have been: it had the topic and threw it away in a
destructuring hole. The function name stays in the message, because it is the only thing
that says where to look.
6. `unreachable` HAS NOW CARRIED BOTH STATUSES, WHICH IS THE WHOLE OF ITS CASE. The kind was
added for tessera.object.anchored and that record is `deferred`, so on one record alone it
read as an escape hatch for emitters blocked elsewhere. tessera.venue.booked is the same
kind and the opposite record — `unfixed`, because every dependency outside micro-tessera
already exists and the repository can close it alone — and the two sit side by side under
one kind without either weakening. An unreferenced emitter says WHERE the estate stopped;
it does not say WHY, and `status` is still the field that answers that. Note 1's rule held
unchanged on its first test: the `until` a `deferred` record owes is a condition SOMEBODY
ELSE must meet, so a gap its owner can close alone cannot have one, and recording this as
`deferred` would have dressed a to-do as a judgement. The evidence is written as a
specification — the three things missing, each with the line that proves it missing —
because the header's warning cuts both ways: an omission reads as neglect and a decision
reads as a decision, and unfinished work is neither. It is work, precisely described.
Keys are '<kind>:<topic>' with kind from the closed set the checker can produce — unemitted,
unregistered, unproduced, stale-record, unreachable. `owner` is the repository whose change
closes it, and must name a repository in the checkout.
$closed: EMPTY IS THE INTENDED STATE, not an unfinished one. Eleven records have been written into this
file and eleven have been deleted by the estate catching up with them, most within a day. Two
went on 2026-08-03, and they are worth naming because the checker cannot tell the two apart —
'the gap is closed, or it has changed shape' — and they were closed in the two different ways
the file argues about at note 2 above:
* `unemitted:ledger.reconciliation.completed` was a MISSING EMIT, and its evidence said so.
micro-ledger wrote one: `RECONCILIATION_COMPLETED` at ledger/src/reconcile.ts:121, emitted
at reconcile.ts:331 keyed `chain:network` as the registry requires, reached from
ledger/src/jobs.ts:222 inside `recurringJobs` — so it satisfies direction 5 as well as
direction 1, which a registered-and-named-but-uncalled emitter would not.
* `unemitted:mint.deploy.confirmed` was a RENAME, and its evidence predicted that: 'this is
the custody shape rather than the ledger one, mint.token.deployed is very probably this
fact under a name nobody else knows'. mint/src/tokens.ts:312 now declares
`DEPLOYED_TOPIC = 'mint.deploy.confirmed'` where it declared the other name, emitted at
tokens.ts:690, and no `mint.token.deployed` survives outside the comments explaining the
change. One repository, no new registrations, no new rules — which is exactly the saving
the custody lesson was written down to secure.
Both were verified against the two repositories' source before deletion rather than against the
exit code, because 'closed' and 'changed shape' produce the same red and only one of them means
the record should go.

unreachable:tessera.object.anchored.evidence: `recordAnchor` (tessera/src/kiln.ts:423) emits OBJECT_ANCHORED at kiln.ts:437 — declared tessera/src/topics.ts:32 — and nothing in tessera/src calls it. IT IS A MISSING CONTRACT, NOT MISSING WIRING, and the emitter's own docstring used to say the opposite: it claimed v1 anchors go 'through the existing mint deploy path', and there is no such path. mint/src/catalogue.ts:28 is the closed union `'fixed' | 'mintable' | 'foundry'`, each variant carrying committed bytecode beside it (:43, :51, :60), with no route that deploys arbitrary bytecode; hearth/contracts/src/ holds HearthV2Router02, Factory, Pair and ERC20, WEMBER and Multicall3, and `grep -ril authorship hearth/` matches NOTHING — the Registry of Authorship Solidity has never been written. So this is not the emitSessionRevoked shape the verdict names it after: that emitter was waiting on a call somebody could have written, and this one is waiting on a chain that does not exist. Deleting it would strand a consumer that is already finished — notify/src/catalogue.ts:1137 is a complete, unblocked rule reading `authorSubject` explicitly, with a template at notify/src/templates.ts:397 and tests at notify/src/catalogue.test.ts:846, and contracts/packages/events/src/audit.ts:323 registers the topic `audited` with `subjectKind: 'user'` — and would take edits in two repositories micro-tessera does not own. The half of this that WAS a defect, no caller AND no test, so the payload's agreement with that waiting consumer was never checked, is closed: tessera/src/kiln.test.ts:479 exercises it against the four fields notify reads. Unwired is a fact about the chain; unverified was a defect, and it is repaired.
unreachable:tessera.object.anchored.until: TWO GREPS, both of which fail today. (1) `hearth/contracts/src/` holds a Registry of Authorship contract — right now `grep -ril authorship hearth/` matches nothing, and the only .sol in the repository are the HearthV2 AMM, WEMBER and Multicall3. (2) `mint` can deploy something that is not one of three ERC-20s — right now `Variant` at mint/src/catalogue.ts:28 is the closed union `'fixed' | 'mintable' | 'foundry'` and every entry of VARIANTS names committed token bytecode, so a registry deploy cannot be expressed at all. When both hold, tessera writes the caller at the seam 04-domain-model §9.3 names — when a creator first LISTS an object, not when they fire it — and this record fails on the next run as one that no longer describes the estate. That failure is the deletion working, not a regression: settlement.outbound.failed and market.offer.made both left this file that way.

unreachable:tessera.venue.booked.evidence: `bookVenue` (tessera/src/economy.ts:516) emits VENUE_BOOKED at economy.ts:549 — declared tessera/src/topics.ts:34 — and outside tests nothing in tessera/src calls it. IT IS UNFINISHED WORK, NOT A DECISION, so it takes no `until`: every dependency outside this repository is already there, and there is nobody to wait for. That is what separates it from the anchor above — micro-ledger serves POST /reservations (ledger/src/server.ts:449) and POST /reservations/:id/release (:488) today, and notify/src/catalogue.ts:1266 is a finished, unblocked `high` rule resolving its recipient through the `ownerSubject` this payload already carries. Nor is it `transferParcel`'s shape: that was a duplicate implementation, consolidated into `moveParcel` (tessera/src/world.ts:711 delegating to :770) so the emitter went live, and no other service in this estate books a venue, so there is nothing to consolidate. WHAT IS MISSING IS THE REST OF THE FEATURE, and wiring the emitter first would be wrong in three separate ways. (1) NO RATE EXISTS ANYWHERE. `parcels.is_venue` is a boolean (tessera/src/migrations.ts:233) with no rate column beside it or in any other table, so `BookInput.priceWei` (economy.ts:501) is an unsourced input and its only constraint is `tessera_booking_price_not_negative check (price_wei >= 0)` (migrations.ts:910) — a zero-price hold on somebody else's calendar is legal today. Who prices a slot is undecided, and a route cannot be written before it is decided. (2) TWO THIRDS OF THE LIFECYCLE HAVE NO CODE. `bookings_status_known` admits `open | settled | cancelled` (migrations.ts:908) and the insert at economy.ts:541 is the ONLY statement against `bookings` in non-test source — there is no `update bookings` in tessera/src at all — so a booking could be opened and never released, STRANDING THE PLAYER'S EMBER IN `reserved`, the account `reservePostings` (tessera/src/ledgerclient.ts:395) posts it to, permanently and with no path out. Money locked with no release is why this emitter must not go live before the other two thirds. (3) `ledger:reserve` (ledger/src/server.ts:80) IS NOT GRANTED. deploy/compose/estate/grant-gaps.json gives `tessera/src/ledgerclient.ts` `ledger:post` alone, derived from 'the single call site: POST /entries ... It reaches no other ledger route'. Real, but explicitly NOT EXTERNAL: the grant is computed from this repository's own call sites, so it opens itself the moment the call site exists. All three are micro-tessera's to write and it needs nobody's permission for any of them, which is exactly why this is `unfixed`. The specification is recorded in full at tessera/README.md:128. The half that WOULD have been a defect is already closed: economy.test.ts:447 exercises the emit against a real database and asserts the outbox row (economy.test.ts:480), and contracts.test.ts:72 pins `keyedBy` to `parcel_id`.
